mil3.1.4:1.2: “This mendicant is wise and capable of conversing with me. I will have many points to ask about, and while those points remain unasked the sun will set. Why don’t I converse with him in the inner palace tomorrow?”
mil3.1.4:2.2: “Well then, Devamantiya, please inform the venerable one: ‘Tomorrow there will be a conversation with the king in the inner palace.’”
mil3.1.4:2.3: Having said this, King Milinda rose from his seat, took leave of the elder Nāgasena, climbed into his chariot, and departed, reciting “Nāgasena, Nāgasena!”
mil3.1.4:3.1: Then Devamantiya said to Venerable Nāgasena—
mil3.1.4:3.3: ‘Tomorrow there will be a conversation with the king in the inner palace.’”
mil3.1.4:3.5: Then, when that night had passed, Devamantiya, Anantakāya, Maṅkura, and Sabbadinna went to King Milinda, and having gone they said to him—
mil3.1.4:3.6: “Great King, shall the venerable Nāgasena come?”
mil3.1.4:3.8: “With how many mendicants shall he come?”
mil3.1.4:3.9: “Let him come with as many mendicants as he wishes.”
mil3.1.4:4.2: “Great King, let him come with ten mendicants.”
mil3.1.4:4.4: “Let him come with as many mendicants as he wishes.”
mil3.1.4:4.6: “Great King, let him come with ten mendicants.”
mil3.1.4:4.8: “Let him come with as many mendicants as he wishes.”
mil3.1.4:4.10: “Great King, let him come with ten mendicants.”
mil3.1.4:4.11: “All this hospitality has been prepared, and I say: ‘Let him come with as many mendicants as he wishes.’
mil3.1.4:4.12: Gentlemen, this Sabbadinna speaks otherwise. Are we not able to give the mendicants a meal?”
mil3.1.4:5.1: Then Devamantiya, Anantakāya, and Maṅkura went to Venerable Nāgasena, and having gone they said to him—
mil3.1.4:5.3: ‘Let him come with as many mendicants as he wishes.’”
mil3.1.4:5.4: Then in the morning Venerable Nāgasena robed up, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāgalā together with eighty thousand mendicants.
mil3.1.4:6.1: Then Anantakāya, walking alongside Venerable Nāgasena, said to him—
mil3.1.4:6.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, when you speak of ‘Nāgasena’, which one here is Nāgasena?”
mil3.1.4:6.5: “Venerable sir, the wind inside, the soul, which enters and leaves—that I consider to be ‘Nāgasena’.”
mil3.1.4:6.6: “If this wind were to go out and not enter again, or enter and not go out, would that person live?”
mil3.1.4:6.8: “And those conch-blowers who blow the conch—does their wind enter again?”
mil3.1.4:6.10: “And those flute-blowers who blow the bamboo flute—does their wind enter again?”
mil3.1.4:6.12: “And those horn-blowers who blow the horn—does their wind enter again?”
mil3.1.4:6.15: “I am not able to converse with a debater like you. Please, venerable sir, explain the meaning.”
mil3.1.4:6.16: “This is not the soul. What are called the in-breath and the out-breath are physical processes.” And the elder gave a talk on the Abhidhamma.
mil3.1.4:6.17: Then Anantakāya declared himself a lay follower.
